description.narrative:
1 Youth Empowerment and Community Engagement on SRHR through sports and physical activity
We will use sports to empower adolescents and youth to understand SRHR topics and increase access to services by linking sports to SRHR training sessions.
2. Increase access to personal, educational and employment opportunities for adolescent girls and boys from Dagoretti and Embakasi through career guidance, talent development and professional training
We will provide training, mentorship and linkages to educational/sports facilities, and peer support for adolescent mothers and boys to improve their long-term career prospects.
3. Gender-Based Violence (GBV) service provision, in Dagoretti and Embakasi
We will expand our integration activities to include hard-to-reach adolescents.

Adolescents in Dagoretti and Embakasi face multiple barriers that affect their immediate and long-term futures. Young people lack knowledge of SRHR topics and struggle to access services. Additionally, there are few support mechanisms and social networks to increase personal wellbeing, educational opportunities and career pathways. Sports is a key entry point to tackling these issues, as it fosters teamwork, relationship building and creates safe spaces. Coaches, teammates and teachers become role models for adolescent youth and impart essential life-skills.
Whilst Phase I achieved strong SRHR outcomes, there is a need to continue the project to reach adolescents not yet supported. Additionally, greater integration of sports and physical activity with training and development opportunities is needed to provide more holistic and sustainable support. In Phase II, we will reach 4,500 adolescent girls and boys in Dagoretti and Embakasi over three years, using sports and physical activity to engage on SRHR topics, provide personal, educational and career development training, and integrate health service provision. New activities in Phase II include supporting boys as well as girls, increasing our focus on hard-to-reach groups such as adolescent mothers and those living in informal settlements, developing our sports provision within schools, improving development pathways for talented athletes, and strengthening the links between sports, life skills and future development.
a) Age range All beneficiaries will be aged between 10 and 19. b) Gender ratio The expected gender split for this project is 83% girls and 17% boys (3,750 girls and 750 boys).
